agl-motion.note: agl-overlay is the only production template that renders the motion COMPONENT; agl-select and agl-multiselect render agl-overlay, so the 'select' and 'multiselect' scenarios construct and tear it down. Note agl-dialog reaches motion through the [aglMotion] DIRECTIVE, which is a different declaration and not in this set

[aglMenuItemContent].note: menu constructs one per item; the 'menu' scenario clicks an item and therefore goes through it

agl-tieredMenuSub.note: each submenu level is one instance; the 'tieredmenu' scenario opens a branch and clicks a nested item

agl-selectItem.note: one per option in the overlay; the 'select' scenario opens the overlay and picks one

li[aglMultiSelectItem].note: one per option in the overlay; the 'multiselect' scenario selects two items

agl-cellEditor.note: in the #sec-table-adv block; the 'table advanced' scenario clicks a cell to switch it from display to input mode

agl-columnFilter.note: in the #sec-table-adv block; the 'table advanced' scenario types then presses Enter, taking the row count from 3 to 1

agl-columnFilterFormElement.note: the real filter input when display=row; it is the field the 'table advanced' scenario types into

[aglTreeTableBody].note: treetable constructs it to render the table body; every visible row goes through it

agl-treeTableToggler.note: the expand/collapse control; the 'treetable' scenario clicks it, taking 1 row to 3. It is NOT rendered by agl-treetable — treetable projects a caller-supplied body template, and apps/verify/src/app.ts puts the toggler in that template itself

agl-treeTableCellEditor.note: in the #sec-treetable-scroll block; the 'treetable scroll + cell edit' scenario clicks a cell and edits the value

[ttScrollableView].note: the #sec-treetable-scroll block enables scrollable; the scenario asserts .p-treetable-scrollable-view exists

agl-table.note: the #sec-table and #sec-table-adv blocks. Covered by scenarios since the gate was written — it entered this manifest only when the guard learned that ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default is the same value as Eager, so the bookkeeping is new, the coverage is not

[aglTableBody].note: table constructs it for both the frozen and the main body, so every visible row in the 'table' and 'table advanced' scenarios goes through it. It is the riskiest of the three: it renders rows from arrays Table mutates in place, which is precisely the update a wrong change-detection strategy drops in silence

agl-scroller.note: the #sec-scroller block, added with this entry — nothing constructed it before, and the four production render sites all sit behind *ngIf="virtualScroll", so claiming transitive coverage through agl-table would have passed the static check while the runtime path stayed unreachable. The 'scroller' scenario scrolls the viewport and reads #probe-scroller, so the assertion is on state that travelled scroll -> component -> output -> view
